ABSTRACT: Herein, we present a copper-catalyzed, three-
component intermolecular 1,4-alkylarylation of 1,3-enynes with
ethers and aryl boronic acids. This method, driven by α-C(sp
3
)−H
functionalization of the oxygen atom in ethers, regioselectively
produces various tetrasubstituted allenes from simple, readily
available precursors. Key features include mild reaction conditions
and a simple catalytic system.
■
INTRODUCTION
Allenes are important structural moieties found in natural
products, bioactive molecules, and material sciences, serving as
valuable intermediates for diverse transformations in synthetic
chemistry.
1
Consequently, numerous efforts have focused on
their construction.
2
Among these, 1,4-difunctionalizations of
readily accessible 1,3-enynes are a powerful and versatile
strategy in organic synthesis to afford multisubstituted allenes.
3
Recently, 1,4-alkylarylation of 1,3-enynes with both alkyl and
aryl groups has garnered increasing interest for its ability to
diversify allene structures.
4
For example, Hong’s group
developed a nickel-catalyzed reductive 1,4-alkylarylation
method for the catalytic conversion of 1,3-enynes into
trisubstituted or tetrasubstituted allenes.
4a
Bao’s group
reported a copper-catalyzed 1,4-alkylarylation of 1,3-enynes
using alkyl diacyl peroxides as masked alkyl electrophiles and
aryl boronic acids as nucleophiles.
4b
Among these reactions,
direct C(sp
3
)−H activation enabling 1,4-difunctionalizations of
1,3-enynes through a radical pathway has gained attention for
its ideal atom and step economy in recent years.
5
In this
context, Kong and co-workers demonstrated a three-
component 1,4-dicarbofunctionalization of 2-trifluoromethyl-
1,3-enynes through selective activation of saturated hydro-
carbons, combining decatungstate photohydrogen atom trans-
fer with nickel catalysis (Scheme 1a).
5a
Subsequently, Li and
co-workers reported a cooperative nickel-photoredox reductive
1,4-dicarbofunctionalization of 1,3-enynes with N-methyl-
amines and organohalides, enabled via site-selective C(sp
3
)−
H functionalization to produce tetrasubstituted allenes
(Scheme 1b).
5b
Despite these advances, there remains a high
demand for facile and efficient methods to construct
multisubstituted allenes from simple, readily available materi-
als.
The construction of carbon−carbon bonds is central to
organic chemistry.
6
Therefore, various classical methods have
been developed for this purpose. Among these, organoboronic
acids are noteworthy as highly effective coupling reagents for
constructing C−C bonds owing to their odorless, stable, safe,
and easy-to-handle solid form.
7
However, methods employing
aromatic boronic acids as coupling reagents for 1,4-
difunctionalization of 1,3-enyne via C(sp
3
)−H functionaliza-
tion remain exceedingly rare.
4b,8
In addition, to the best of our
knowledge, a copper-catalyzed 1,4-alkylarylation of 1,3-enynes
enabled via C(sp
3
)−H functionalization has not been reported.
In line with our ongoing interests in 1,4-difunctionalizations of
1,3-enynes,
9
we herein report a copper-catalyzed 1,4-
alkylarylation of 1,3-enynes with ethers and aryl boronic
acids, facilitated via C(sp
3
)−H functionalization (Scheme 1c).
■

Under the identified optimal reaction conditions (Table 1,
entry 6), the substrate compatibility of the current copper-
catalyzed 1,4-alkylarylation of 1,3-enynes was investigated. As
shown in Table 2, various 1,3-enynes were tested. Substituents
on the aromatic ring of the alkenyl moiety, including F, Cl, Br,
Me, and OMe at the ortho, meta, and para positions, were
tolerated, affording the corresponding products 4b−4j in 30−
54% yields. The alkynyl moiety of 1,3-enyne was also
investigated, with propyl, n-hexyl, or cyclopropyl substitutions
providing products 4k−4m in 30−56% yields. Additionally,
1,3-enynes bearing alkyl substituents on both the alkynyl and
alkenyl moieties, such as 2-methylhex-1-en-3-yne 1n, were
compatible and afforded the corresponding product 4n. When

yl)benzene 1o, the reaction produced the desired product 4o
in a 30% yield, probably owing to steric hindrance.
4b
Notably,
sulfur-containing heteroaromatic substrates 1p and 1q also
participated in the reaction, forming the corresponding
products 4p and 4q in 32% and 31% yields, respectively.

to a diverse range of aryl boronic acids (Table 3). As expected,
various aryl boronic acids bearing different functional groups
were well tolerated, yielding the corresponding products in
moderate yields. Halo-substituted aryl boronic acids were

minimal effect on yield, with products 5b and 5d isolated in

After successfully exploring the scope of 1,3-enynes and aryl
boronic acids, we also examined variations of ethers (Table 4).
As expected, the reaction proceeded smoothly with similar
cyclic ethers, such as tetrahydropyran and 1,4-dioxane,
affording the desired products 6b and 6c in 50 and 49%
yields, respectively. Notably, expanding the scope to acyclic
ethers also proved to be successful, yielding the corresponding
allenes 6d and 6e.
To demonstrate the practical utility of this protocol, a
scaled-up reaction was conducted. Satisfyingly, using 1.0 mmol
of oct-1-en-3-yn-2-ylbenzene (1a) and (4-fluorophenyl)-
boronic acid (2g) produced 5g in 34% yield (Scheme 2).
A preliminary mechanistic investigation suggested that the
reaction probably proceeded via a radical reaction pathway.
This copper-catalyzed 1,4-alkylarylation of 1,3-enynes was
completely inhibited when the radical scavenger 2,2,6,6-
tetramethyl-1-piperidinyloxy (TEMPO) was introduced
(Scheme 3).
Based on the results and related literature, a plausible
mechanism is proposed (Scheme 4). Initially, tert-butylperoxy
(
t
BuOO
•
) and tert-butoxyl (
t
BuO
•
) radicals are generated from
TBHP decomposition facilitated by the copper catalyst.
10
Subsequently, these radicals abstract a hydrogen atom from
THF, forming ether radical A,
11
which reacts with 1,3-enynes
to yield propargyl radical B and its resonance structure, allenyl
radical C. Meanwhile, Cu(II) species undergo transmetalation
with aryl boronic acid 2a, affording aryl−Cu(II).
4b,12
Then,
aryl−Cu(II) interacts with allenyl radical species C to form
Cu(III) intermediate D. Finally, reductive elimination of the
Cu(III) intermediate forms the desired product 4a and
regenerates Cu(I) species,
4b
which are oxidized to Cu(II) to
sustain the next catalytic cycle.

■
CONCLUSIONS
Herein, we developed a copper-catalyzed three-component
1,4-alkylarylation of 1,3-enynes with ethers and aryl boronic
acids via C(sp
3
)−H functionalization. This methodology
provides a novel method for constructing tetrasubstituted
allenes. The developed method is characterized by mild
reaction conditions, readily available starting materials, and a
simple catalytic system. Ongoing efforts in our group aim to
elucidate the detailed reaction mechanism and extend this
strategy to the synthesis of multisubstituted allenes.
■
